pl-l4d50c1-d1e134.summary: Quotes Augustine: God gave men only this life to gain eternal life, in which he willed penance to be fruitful, since here one can put off malice, change his will, merits, and works, and do what pleases God. Whoever does not do so here will have repentance of his evils in the future world but find no pardon before the Lord, since though there will be the sting of repentance, there will be no correction of will; they will blame their iniquity but never love or desire justice; their will will always bear the punishment of its malignity and never receive good affection; as those reigning with Christ will have no remnant of evil will, those condemned to eternal fire with the devil will have no rest nor good will.
claims: Merit and fruitful penance belong to this life only.
The damned feel remorse without amendment of will.
They can never have a good will.

pl-l4d50c1.summary: Asks how Augustine can say the damned lack the power to sin, since they keep an evil will. Some say that evil will is not sin but only punishment; others that it is sin but merits no punishment, there being no place for merit, so it is the punishment of prior evil merit. Augustine: the time to gain eternal life and fruitful penance is only this life; those who do not repent here will feel remorse hereafter but find no pardon, since there will be no correction of will; their will always bears the punishment of its malice and can never receive good affection. So the reprobate will repent without abandoning their evil will, which increases their punishment without merit, since no one merits except in this life.
claims: The damned keep an evil will.
That evil will is punishment of prior merit, not a new merit.
Merit and fruitful penance are possible only in this life.
The damned feel remorse but cannot amend their will.
